record.original_question:
A sequence {γ_k}_{k≥0} is called a complex zero decreasing sequence
(CZDS) if, for every real polynomial Σ a_k x^k,
applying the diagonal coefficient multiplier gives a polynomial Σ γ_k
a_k x^k with no more nonreal zeros than the
original one. Characterize all such complex zero decreasing sequences.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real polynomial $p(x) = \sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k$, let $Z_c(p)$ denote the number of nonreal zeros of $p$, counted with multiplicity. A sequence of real numbers $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is called a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS) if, for every real polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k$ (of arbitrary degree $n$), the diagonal coefficient multiplier produces a polynomial whose nonreal zero count does not exceed that of the original:
$$Z_c\!\left(\sum_{k=0}^n \gamma_k a_k x^k\right) \;\le\; Z_c\!\left(\sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k\right).$$
Give a complete characterization of all complex zero decreasing sequences $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The full characterization of complex zero decreasing sequences (closely tied to the Karlin–Laguerre problem on multiplier sequences) is widely cited as a long-standing open problem. Craven and Csordas characterized those CZDS that can be interpolated by real polynomials, and various special cases are known, but no general characterization exists.

status_evidence.title: Complex Zero Decreasing Sequences — Craven & Csordas
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of CZDS interpolated by polynomials; general characterization not known.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial classifications of CZDS are available.

status_evidence.title: Composition theorems, multiplier sequences and complex zero decreasing sequences (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: The Karlin–Laguerre problem of characterizing CZDS has eluded researchers for over four decades.
status_evidence.claim: The general characterization of CZDS remains open.
